annual_return.description: geometric (CAGR): (prod(1 + r))^(periods_per_year / n) - 1; the arithmetic mean x periods_per_year is reported separately

annualization.scaling: square-root-of-time for volatility; linear for arithmetic means
annualization.unknown: not annualized unless the caller declares the observation frequency

benchmark.appraisal_ratio: annualized OLS alpha / annualized residual volatility
benchmark.batting_average: share of aligned periods with fund return strictly above benchmark
benchmark.capture: geometric, annualized over up (benchmark > 0) or down (benchmark < 0) periods
benchmark.capture_ratio: upside capture / downside capture; undefined unless downside capture > 0
benchmark.description: periods aligned on their intersection (monthly/quarterly/yearly by calendar period, daily/weekly by exact date); missing benchmark returns are never filled
benchmark.information_ratio: annualized arithmetic mean active return / tracking error
benchmark.m_squared: aligned Sharpe ratio x benchmark volatility, arithmetic annualization
benchmark.regime_betas: OLS with intercept on benchmark > 0 (bull) or < 0 (bear) periods
benchmark.regression: OLS of fund on benchmark returns (risk-free = 0)
benchmark.residual_volatility: OLS regression standard error (m - 2 dof) x sqrt(periods_per_year)
benchmark.timing_ratio: bull beta / bear beta; undefined unless bear beta > 0

charts.bar_baseline: bars always grow from zero; the value axis always includes zero
charts.benchmark: compared only over the aligned overlap, both rebased to 1.0 at its start
charts.episode_table: deepest drawdown episodes first (ties: earliest peak); all in JSON
charts.heatmap_scale: diverging, symmetric around zero at the largest absolute month
charts.histogram_bins: Freedman-Diaconis width clipped to 10 to 40 bins over the range; edges then aligned at zero, which can add one bin
charts.history: every chart spans the full analyzed history; no start date is chosen
charts.partial_years: shown outlined and labelled partial; never styled as full years
charts.rolling_windows: the one-year windows of the rolling metrics (rolling.*)
charts.wealth_scale: linear, starting at 1.0 one period before the first return

distribution.description: bias-corrected sample estimators G1 and G2 (as pandas / Excel)

downside.description: target (MAR) = 0% per period; downside deviation = sqrt(sum(min(r - MAR, 0)^2) / n) using all n observations

drawdown.description: wealth index starts at 1 before the first return, so a first-period loss is a drawdown; drawdowns reported as signed returns (negative = loss)

factor_model.alignment: periods where the fund and every factor have a return; never filled
factor_model.covariance: Newey-West HAC, Bartlett kernel, small-sample factor m / (m - k - 1)
factor_model.estimator: OLS with intercept of fund (excess) returns on the supplied factors
factor_model.inference: Student t with m - k - 1 degrees of freedom
factor_model.risk_free: a factor column named RF is subtracted from fund returns; without one the dependent variable is the fund return (risk-free rate 0%)

missing_data.description: missing returns are never replaced by zero or forward-filled; leading and trailing gaps are trimmed, interior gaps are disclosed and the remaining observations are analyzed

ocr.header_inference: up to three month headers the engine misread are placed by the column spacing of the others (recorded)
ocr.line_grouping: words overlapping vertically by at least half the smaller height

outliers.description: robust z-score |r - median| / (1.4826 * MAD) above 5 is flagged (never removed)

risk_free.description: 0% per period in methodology 0.1.0 for all excess-return metrics (Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, Martin, alpha, Treynor). Ratios are therefore total-return ratios; this is disclosed on every affected metric.

serial_correlation.sharpe_adjustment: Lo (2002): SR_per_period * q / sqrt(q + 2 * sum_{k=1}^{q-1} (q-k) rho_k)

sharpe_inference.moments: population skewness g1 and non-excess kurtosis m4 / m2^2

smoothing.reference: Getmansky, Lo & Makarov (2004), Journal of Financial Economics 74(3)

tail.description: historical 95% VaR = 5% empirical quantile (linear interpolation, R type 7); 95% ES = mean of returns at or below that quantile; both reported as signed returns (negative = loss)

min_data_policies.description: Observed fact about the supplied history; any non-empty history suffices.
Path statistics (drawdowns, streaks) are computable from one observation but are unrepresentative below 3 years (low) and 5 years (moderate); longer histories tend to reveal deeper drawdowns.
Mean-type estimates: low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5 years.
Requires at least 2 observations; low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5.
Risk-adjusted ratios: at least 2 observations; low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5 years.
Requires at least 3 observations; standard error is roughly sqrt(6/n), so low confidence below 60 and moderate below 120 observations.
Requires at least 4 observations; kurtosis estimates are highly unstable, so low confidence below 120 and moderate below 240 observations.
Requires at least 2 observations; low confidence when fewer than 5 observations are expected in the 5% tail (n < 100), moderate when fewer than 10 (n < 200).
Requires at least 5 observations; standard error is roughly 1/sqrt(n), so low confidence below 36 and moderate below 60 observations.
Requires at least 10 observations for a 3-lag test; low below 36, moderate below 60.
Asymptotic Sharpe-ratio inference needs at least 4 observations for the moments it uses; the normal approximation is poor below 36 observations (low) and 60 (moderate).
Requires at least 3 aligned observations; low confidence below 3 years of overlap, moderate below 5 years.
Requires at least 2 aligned observations; low confidence below 3 years of overlap, moderate below 5 years.

One-year-horizon serial-correlation statistics need at least two years of data (undefined below); their standard error is about sqrt(4 / (3 y)) for y years, so confidence is low below 5 years and moderate below 10 years.
Requires at least 3 aligned observations and at least k + 2 for k factors (k + 1 coefficients and one residual degree of freedom); low confidence below 3 years of overlap, moderate below 5 years.
